text:
Erin: Hey team — customer ACME reported a ~30m spike of 502/504 errors from Hosted API (eu1) between 10:12–10:42 UTC. They attached a curl sample and trace ids. Can someone triage? :eyes:
Erin: curl they used:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{\"input\":\"short prompt\"}'
```
Erin: sample trace: trace_id=txf-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h, proxy logs show upstream reset + \"502\" returned from env->upstream with upstream_reset_reason=HTTP2_STREAM_CLOSED
DeployBot: incident alert created: INC-2026-091 (severity: high) — auto-tags: edge-gateway, http2, auth
Omar: Thanks Erin — looking at ingress metrics now. I see an authcache eviction spike at 10:10 that correlates with increased upstream connection churn. qps steady though.
Lee: Can you paste the envoy logs for txf-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h? Also need upstream host pool stats (keepalive_active, conn_window) from that timeframe.
Erin: pasted logs from edge-proxy-12:
```
[10:15:12] envoy upstream reset: upstream_reset_reason=HTTP2_RST_STREAM
[10:15:12] stream closed before response: downstream_local_close
[10:15:13] returning 502 to client, route: /v1/generate, tenant=acme
```
Omar: Hypothesis: h2 keepalive mismatch + too many concurrent streams on a pooled upstream causing stream resets under authcache reload. We saw similar pattern with large-embeds burst earlier.
Jamie: Customer says this happens during heavy short-stream bursts (many tiny requests). They also use connection-reuse in their client. Could be windowing or MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS saturation on the upstream cluster.
Lee: Quick mitigation: temporarily pin ACME traffic to a separate backend pool or reduce client-side concurrency. I'll open a short-lived routing override to send ACME to pool-b while we debug.
Erin: Customer accepted workaround — applied header route to pool-b at 10:25 UTC. Errors dropped to baseline around 10:28.
Omar: Good signal. Next steps: capture tcpdump for a reproduce window and enable envoy upstream debug for h2 flow control. Also check authcache reload frequency — looks like ttl bounce at 10:09 triggered mass revalidation.
Erin: Repro steps requested from customer: ramp many small requests (50r/s) with keepalive reuse for 3m using the curl-loop below. They tested and observed failures.
Erin: repro script:
```
for i in $(seq 1 900); do \
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" -d '{\"input\":\"p\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\n  sleep 0.06\ndone\nwait\n```
Omar: Can someone run the above in staging (eu1-staging) with tcpdump on upstream to capture h2 frame resets? Use a low rate first to avoid noisy impact.
Lee: I'll collect envoy stats: cluster.acme_upstream.http2.* (active_streams, connection_transient_failure, downstream_cx_rx_bytes_total) and increase upstream max concurrent streams temporarily to test.
Jamie: Also add an eval to Redwood Optimize to see if batching suggestions would reduce tiny-request churn for this customer. Not a fix for gateway but reduces load.
Omar: TL;DR: Root cause likely env->upstream HTTP/2 stream resets triggered by concurrent stream saturation combined with authcache evictions. Workaround (routing to pool-b) reduced errors. Next: capture packet traces, adjust upstream settings, and harden authcache reloads.
Erin: I'll keep the customer updated and request pcap + timing when they next reproduce. Thanks all :thumbsup:
